# s234 — Render in the same step when next --start claims an item

`next --start` is a mutation that cannot render, so every documented pickup that uses it leaves `.slicer/render/` stale.

**Findings:** session 2026-10-07: landing s233, the documented review pickup (next --status review --start) moved s233 to reviewing and left ROADMAP.md and ROADMAP.html stale; slicer check failed until a manual slicer render. next has no --render because cmd_next is not wrapped in _mutating · **Size:** S · **Tree:** slicer

**2026-10-07** — Ready for review: next gains --render/--strict (only with --start; else usage). cmd_next takes the writer lock for --render and runs _select_next through _mutating; a pickup that changes nothing sets _no_change so it skips the render; batch lock now follows an explicit locked flag. Pickup commands in ai.py, AGENTS.md, docs updated; SKILL.md regenerated. New tests/test_next_render.py (10). Full suite 1493: 1 failure, test_AgentsGuide_RoadmapSection_IsShorter (4213+ bytes vs 3800 cap), already failing on main since 7c47623 (3772 before it); not caused by this slice.

trust: unverified; by: Jon Robbins

**Not in this slice:** rendering on read-only `next`, a config default that renders after every mutation, or changing `next` payloads.

## Why

`next --start` changes state: it claims an item and moves it to started, or moves a review item to reviewing. Unlike `start`, it has no `--render`, because `cmd_next` is registered without `_mutating` (`cli.py:2635`). S45 gave mutating commands `--render` but did not cover `next`.

Observed 2026-10-07 while landing s233: the reviewer pickup in AGENTS.md, `next --status review --start --ready --section "Check" --json --lean`, moved s233 to reviewing. The next `slicer check` then failed with stale `ROADMAP.md` and `ROADMAP.html` until `slicer render` was run by hand. The skill's combined pickup (`ai.py` step 1, `next --start --ready ...`) and the handoff section's reviewer command (`ai.py:237`) have the same gap. An agent following the instructions exactly gets a red check that is only staleness, which is what S45 set out to remove.

## Files

- `src/slicer/cli.py`: register `next` through `_strict_flag(_render_flag(...))` and `_mutating`, and reject `--render` without `--start` in `cmd_next`.
- `src/slicer/ai.py`: add `--render` to the `next --start` commands in the loop (step 1) and in `HANDOFF_SECTION`.
- `skills/slicer/SKILL.md`: regenerate from `ai.skill_text()`.
- `AGENTS.md`: add `--render` to the reviewer pickup command under "Landing a slice".
- `docs/commands.md` and `docs/agents.md`: add `[--render] [--strict]` to the `next` usage and say they apply only with `--start`.
- Tests next to the existing `next --start` tests (`tests/test_next.py`, `tests/test_next_queue.py`, `tests/test_next_batch.py`).

## Failing tests

- `next --start --render` on an open item claims it and leaves `slicer check` passing, with no separate `render`.
- `next --status review --start --render` moves a review item to reviewing and leaves `slicer check` passing.
- `next --batch K --start --render` starts every returned id and renders once.
- `next --render` without `--start` is `usage` and writes nothing.
- `next --start --render` with no eligible item exits 2 with the usual `{"item": null, "blocked": [...]}` payload and does not render.
- Resuming an item already started or claimed by the caller (which writes nothing) does not render or report a change.
- `next --start --render --strict` follows the render-first policy of the other mutations: a render failure rolls the claim back.
- `--json` stdout stays the single `next` document in every case above.

## Implement

Register `next` the way `start` is registered (`cli.py:2848`), so `--render` and `--strict` go through `_mutating` and cannot drift from the other commands. In `cmd_next`, treat `--render` without `--start` as `usage`, the same way `--owner` without `--start` is handled. When a start or resume writes nothing, set `args._no_change` so `_mutating` skips the render. `cmd_next` takes its own lock for `--start`. Confirm that `_mutate_strict` and `_render_after_mutation` do not deadlock or double-lock with it, and that the exit 2 "no item" path returns before any render.

Then add `--render` to the documented pickup commands listed in Files and regenerate the skill. Read-only `next` output and payloads stay the same.
